title: Fail-closed no-egress guard + local_only scope marking + egress_posture MCP tool + .well-known capability publication
priority_note: Highest-value story in the epic. #331 shipped agent autonomy over KB content while egress stayed uncontrolled AND undiscoverable - an agent can harvest a DNA file today with no supported way to check where it goes first. This story closes that, and it is the one capability that cannot be replaced by careful configuration. It therefore does NOT wait on US-41.2/US-41.3: the classifier, the fail-closed guard and egress_posture are implementable against TODAY's resolved (hardcoded vendor) endpoints, and posture reporting is strictly more truthful early. It is extended, not rewritten, as 41.2/41.3 make endpoints configurable.
background: Loopctl.Provider.Admission (lib/loopctl/provider/admission.ex, US-37.1 / GH #352) already sits immediately before every model-provider Req.post: anthropic.ex:118 guards :139, embedding_client.ex:91 and :101 guard :109 and :133. That makes it the correct chokepoint. CRITICALLY it is FAIL-OPEN BY DESIGN (admission.ex:81-97, fail_open/2 at :183) - it is a burst shedder whose job is to shed load without ever blocking legitimate traffic. An egress guard needs the OPPOSITE failure semantics. Fusing the two decisions would mean a Hammer or SystemConfig hiccup silently degrades the privacy guarantee to 'allow', turning a guarantee into a hope. The guard must therefore be a SEPARATE check at the same call sites that cannot inherit the fail-open path. Two grounded constraints shape the design: (a) Admission itself was added site-by-site and is consequently MISSED at webhooks/req_delivery.ex:43, verification/github_actions.ex:17 and secrets/fly_adapter.ex:60,112 - a guarantee enforced by per-call-site convention regresses the first time someone adds a Req call; (b) UrlGuard (net/url_guard.ex, GHSA-jh42-wf7g-f5rg) blocks loopback and every private range unconditionally, so the SSRF policy and the locality policy must be one module, not two that contradict each other.

story.as_a: an agent about to harvest a user's private documents
story.i_want_to: mark the target scope local_only, have loopctl HARD-REFUSE any provider call that would send that data to a non-local endpoint, and query the instance's egress posture before I start
story.so_that: private data cannot leave the boundary by misconfiguration or by a wrong base_url, and I can verify locality first instead of trusting it

rationale: A privacy tier that depends on the operator configuring three endpoints correctly is not a guarantee. Fail-closed enforcement plus a machine-readable posture surface converts it into one an agent can verify - which is the only form that works on a platform with no UI.

acceptance_criteria.description: A local_only marking exists at tenant and project scope, settable via a new MCP tool + matching JSON API endpoint (no UI). Default off everywhere; the hosted instance behaves exactly as today until a scope opts in. ROLES ARE ASYMMETRIC because the two transitions are not symmetric in trust: ENABLING local_only (tightening) is role :orchestrator or above, while DISABLING/CLEARING it is role :user - clearing the flag is exactly the self-widening move AC-41.4.5 forbids for the allowlist, and it would let an agent re-open egress one tool call before a harvest while US-41.7's witnessed claim faithfully attested the weakened posture. Both transitions are recorded in the audit log with actor and scope. Tests assert NO agent-role path clears local_only through any tool or endpoint. BECAUSE the enabling role cannot undo the transition, ENABLE CARRIES A MANDATORY PRE-FLIGHT, mirroring AC-41.5.4's duty for webhook subscriptions (provider endpoints are the higher-impact case, so the weaker treatment was backwards): before the flag is set, the currently-resolved embedding and chat endpoints for the scope are classified, and if any of them would become egress_blocked the operation either REFUSES with a remediation naming each offending endpoint, or completes only when the caller passes an explicit acknowledgement flag and REPORTS the resulting blocked posture in the response. Which of the two is chosen is documented. A silent enable that instantly stops all embedding, extraction, classification, merge and (per US-41.5) webhook delivery for a tenant - undoable only by a human :user key - is not acceptable: for the default tenant, which has configured no local endpoint, that is a tenant-wide outage triggered by an orchestrator-role or compromised dispatch key. Every enable ALSO emits a high-priority audit event and an alertable telemetry event naming the actor, the scope and the count of endpoints that became blocked.

Scope resolution is defined, not left per-call-site: the effective marking is the MOST RESTRICTIVE of the tenant and project markings (project local_only OR tenant local_only), a project can NEVER relax a tenant-level local_only, and any row or operation with no project (articles.project_id is nullable = tenant-wide, article.ex:19; memories have no required project association) inherits the TENANT marking. Because the guarded call sites carry no project context today (EmbeddingClient.generate_embedding/2 and Llm.Anthropic.call/N reach Admission with tenant_id only), the scope is THREADED through the embedding and chat APIs by this story. ENDPOINT RESOLUTION IS TENANT-SCOPED ONLY. The round-1 text's 'project settings override tenant settings' clause is REMOVED: no story in this epic defines a project_llm_settings table, its RLS, its role gate or its precedence rule, so that clause was a load-bearing resolution rule with no owning data model - it would have been improvised at implementation time inside the module that gates egress, and a project-scoped endpoint override written at orchestrator role would let an agent-orchestrator redirect a project's extraction to an endpoint of its choosing, which is exactly why US-41.2 AC-41.2.2 keeps endpoint writes at role :user. CONSEQUENCE, stated rather than hidden: a local_only PROJECT inside a tenant whose endpoints are vendor defaults is egress_blocked, and the documented remediation is to configure a satisfying endpoint AT TENANT level (role :user) or to clear the project marking. Project-scoped endpoints, if ever wanted, are a separate story with their own schema, RLS, role and security argument. A test covers each combination: project-marked, tenant-marked, both, neither, and project-less, plus the blocked-project remediation text.

When a scope is local_only, every outbound model-provider call whose resolved endpoint is not classified local is refused with {:error, :egress_blocked} BEFORE the Req.post. The check is FAIL-CLOSED: if the endpoint cannot be classified, or if the classification machinery itself errors, the call is REFUSED. A test forces the classifier to raise and asserts the call is blocked, not admitted. OBAN SEMANTICS ARE PART OF THIS AC, not left to the worker author: :egress_blocked is a PERMANENT configuration refusal, so every Oban worker that can receive it (embedding, extraction, classification, merge, re-embed) maps it to {:cancel, :egress_blocked} - NEVER {:error, _} (which Oban retries, burning max_attempts with backoff on every item and repopulating the queue on every subsequent write) and never {:snooze, _}. This mirrors the terminal treatment US-41.5 TC-41.5.5 requires for blocked webhook deliveries. A test enqueues a batch against a permanently blocked scope and asserts no retry backlog accumulates.

The guard is a SEPARATE decision from Provider.Admission's fail-open rate check, and it is enforced at a SINGLE MANDATORY CHOKEPOINT rather than by per-call-site convention: all tenant-content egress routes through one wrapper (a Req request step or a Loopctl.Provider.post/3 wrapper) that performs the check, and a static test or Credo check asserts no direct outbound HTTP call exists in the scanned paths outside that wrapper's explicit allowlist. THE CHECK'S SURFACE IS ENUMERATED, and so is its RESIDUAL GAP, because the round-1 wording ('mandatory, not conventional') was broader than the three Req functions it named. (i) Detected entry points: Req.post / Req.request / Req.get / Req.put / Req.patch / Req.delete / Req.new AND Req.Request.run/run_request, plus Finch.request/Finch.build, Mint.HTTP.*, :httpc.request, :gen_tcp.connect and :ssl.connect. (ii) The scanned path list is CONFIGURABLE (default lib/), so the negative-control fixture can live under test/support and still be scanned - a fixture outside the scanned paths makes the negative control a no-op. (iii) RESIDUAL GAP, documented in the AC and in the docs rather than papered over: the check cannot see HTTP performed INSIDE a dependency, and it does not cover the separate mcp-server/ codebase. The guarantee wording everywhere (docs, tool descriptions, custody claim) is narrowed to the paths actually proven: 'every outbound HTTP call made by loopctl application code'. Admission's fail_open/2 path can never admit a call the egress guard would refuse. A test asserts that with the admission backend fully unavailable (fail-open triggered), a local_only scope with a non-local endpoint is still BLOCKED, and a second test adds a raw call for EACH detected entry point to a fixture module inside the scanned path list and asserts the static check FAILS on every one - proving the check is load-bearing in both directions.

Locality classification separates the two concepts the epic must not conflate - NETWORK locality and TENANT OWNERSHIP: (a) network-local means loopback and private-range hosts plus the deployment LOCAL_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST; (b) tenant-declared trusted endpoints are a PER-TENANT list of hosts the tenant attests are their own (their VPS, tailscale funnel, or domain), settable at role :user only. This second list is mandatory, not optional: on the HOSTED instance the server's loopback and private ranges are the OPERATOR's network, so a hosted tenant's own Ollama/TEI box is reachable ONLY via a public hostname, and a network-locality-only definition would hard-block every real hosted local_only tenant - contradicting the epic's central claim that Axis A ships on the hosted service unchanged. THREE HARD CONSTRAINTS ON DECLARATIONS, all enforced, because this list is tenant-writable at role :user and would otherwise be a self-service SSRF primitive into the operator network (the class GHSA-jh42-wf7g-f5rg closed): (1) PUBLIC ADDRESSES ONLY. A declaration is REJECTED AT WRITE TIME, and re-checked at pin time, unless every address the host resolves to still passes UrlGuard's full denylist - loopback, 0/8, 10/8, 127/8, 169.254/16 (incl. 169.254.169.254), 172.16-31, 192.168, 100.64/10 and fdaa::/16 may NEVER be declared, whether given literally or reached via a public hostname that resolves there (url_guard.ex:254-261). This costs the use case nothing: the paragraph above establishes that a hosted tenant's box is reachable only by public hostname, so the private-range carve-out is not needed for the case that justifies the list. Private/link-local/CGNAT/6PN carve-outs are available ONLY through the operator-controlled deployment allowlist. (2) PURPOSE-SCOPED. Each declaration names its purposes (inference and/or webhook); a host declared for an Ollama box does NOT authorize US-41.5 webhook POSTs of tenant content to it. One list must not be an ambient capability across subsystems. (3) VENDOR HOSTS EXCLUDED: api.openai.com and api.anthropic.com are never local and may never be declared - and this two-name check is understood to be a guardrail against the obvious mistake, NOT an integrity control (it is trivially defeated by a proxy, a CNAME or any other vendor), which is why constraints (1) and (2) carry the actual security weight. A DECLARATION IS AN UNVERIFIED TENANT ATTESTATION, not a verified control: loopctl does not prove the declaring tenant owns the host. The posture report and the US-41.7 custody claim LABEL the two distinctly ('network-local' vs 'tenant-declared (unverified attestation), not network-local'), must never present a declared endpoint as network-local, and the README, the local_only tool description and the custody-claim wording carry that qualifier verbatim. The deployment allowlist remains DEPLOYMENT-scoped and READ-ONLY to every role including :user - it is the trust root, and an agent must never widen its own allowlist; a test asserts no API path mutates it.

egress_blocked degrades safely and legibly WITHOUT poisoning the circuit breaker: Knowledge.breaker_countable?/1 gains an explicit clause returning FALSE for :egress_blocked (knowledge.ex:7941's catch-all returns true today, so a brand-new atom would record a provider failure toward the per-tenant breaker and emit the fleet-wide [:loopctl, :llm, :provider_error] storm signal - exactly the failure :rate_limited_local was exempted for at :7939). A permanent local configuration refusal must never open the breaker. The interactive path falls back like the existing circuit-open case (keyword search, never a 500); harvesting fails the ITEM with an agent-readable reason naming the scope and the offending endpoint. A test asserts a blocked call records no provider-error telemetry and never opens the breaker. No data is sent in any path. REMOVING the provider_error signal for blocked calls must not leave operators blind, so a DEDICATED replacement metric is added in the same change: a [:loopctl, :egress, :blocked] telemetry event (measurement: count; metadata: tenant_id, scope, endpoint host, reason) plus an aggregate blocked-rate counter, so a tenant that has been silently non-functional since an enable is visible on the existing dashboards. AUDIT WRITE AMPLIFICATION IS BOUNDED: blocked decisions are cheap and happen before any network call, so a single misconfigured harvest loop would otherwise write thousands of audit rows per minute. Audit records for blocked decisions are therefore DEDUPLICATED/AGGREGATED per (scope, endpoint, reason, time window) - one record per window carrying an occurrence count, not one per call - while the telemetry counter carries the exact per-call rate. A test drives N blocked calls in one window and asserts a bounded number of audit rows and an accurate counter.

The degraded response is explicitly labelled and never a bare empty list. Whenever the semantic path is unavailable (egress_blocked, circuit open, or embedding fallback), the response meta names the reason AND the offending endpoint. THIS STORY delivers the meta CONTRACT including a reserved, extensible excluded_tiers field; the encrypted-tier clause that populates it is delivered and TESTED IN US-41.6 (AC-41.6.5, TC-41.6.3), not here, because encrypt_body is introduced by US-41.6 - which depends on US-41.4 - so a cross-story test asserting both flags at once cannot exist at the time US-41.4 is verified. Rationale for keeping the contract here: US-41.6 AC-41.6.4 removes encrypted bodies from the FTS index, so without the field a local_only + encrypt_body tenant would receive a successful-looking 200 with a structurally impossible-to-populate result set that reads as 'nothing in your KB'. A test in THIS story asserts the meta names the reason and the offending endpoint and that excluded_tiers is present (empty until US-41.6 populates it) - never a bare empty list.

An egress_posture MCP tool + matching JSON endpoint reports: the resolved embedding and chat endpoints for the calling tenant, the locality VERDICT for each (network-local / tenant-declared (unverified attestation) / non-local), the tenant's own declared trusted endpoints with their purposes, and per-scope local_only and encrypt_body status. It ALSO reports named POSTURE DEFECTS, of which encrypt_body enabled on a scope that is not local_only ('encrypted_at_rest_plaintext_in_flight', US-41.6 AC-41.6.13) is the first. Endpoints are shown; keys never are. THE DEPLOYMENT ALLOWLIST'S CONTENTS ARE NOT DISCLOSED AT AGENT ROLE: it is operator-plane infrastructure state (internal hostnames/CIDRs of the hosted deployment) and it is precisely the target list an SSRF attacker wants, so shipping it to the lowest-privileged key of every tenant contradicts this AC's own classification of the allowlist as the trust root. At :agent the payload carries only the caller's own endpoints and their verdicts (which is all verify-before-harvest needs) plus a boolean saying whether the verdict came from the allowlist; the allowlist CONTENTS are returned only at role :user and above. This is how an agent verifies locality BEFORE harvesting. It is a READ tool available at agent role.

There is exactly ONE egress policy module and every outbound path consults it: the provider guard, the US-41.2 probe, ingestion, and (in US-41.5) webhook delivery. It composes the SSRF denylist with the locality decision, and THE CARVE-OUT POWERS ARE SPLIT BY PLANE - the round-1 text granted both lists the same power, which handed every :user-role tenant an SSRF hole into the operator's network: (a) the OPERATOR-CONTROLLED deployment allowlist (migration/operator plane, unwritable at every role per AC-41.4.5) is the ONLY thing that can carve specific hosts/CIDRs out of UrlGuard's loopback/private/CGNAT/link-local/Fly-6PN denylist; (b) TENANT-DECLARED trusted endpoints carve NOTHING out of that denylist - they only change the LOCALITY verdict for hosts that already pass it (public addresses, per AC-41.4.5 constraint 1), and each is honoured only for its declared purposes (constraint 2). GHSA-jh42-wf7g-f5rg therefore stays closed for every tenant-writable input. A second, divergent URL policy anywhere in lib/ is a review failure. Tests: a tenant CANNOT declare or reach a private-range / link-local / 6PN host (169.254.169.254, 10/8, 127/8, 100.64/10, fdaa::/16) whether given literally or via a public hostname that resolves there; a host in the deployment allowlist IS reachable; and a host declared for 'inference' only is refused for webhook delivery.

The .well-known/loopctl discovery endpoint (US-26.0.4) publishes instance CAPABILITIES: the FIXED set of supported embedding dimensions (US-41.1 AC-41.1.3), whether tenant-supplied endpoints are permitted, and which tiers exist - so an agent can discover the instance's constraints BEFORE authenticating. No tenant-specific data appears there.

Every new table or column introduced by this story (local_only markings, declared trusted endpoints, egress-decision records) carries tenant_id, uses the enable_rls/1 macro (ENABLE, not FORCE, per CLAUDE.md's Multi-Tenant Rules), and has a tenant-isolation test asserting tenant A cannot read or mutate tenant B's marking. Deployment-scoped state (the allowlist) is explicitly NOT tenant data and lives outside RLS by design.

Hot-path cost is one cheap classification per provider call with NO network or DB round-trip, and the resolution, ownership, refresh and invalidation policy is stated rather than left open. RESOLUTION: the endpoint host is resolved and classified into a pinned IP set, cached with a TTL, and the call-time check reads that cache and connects with UrlGuard.pinned_request_opts/1 so the IP actually connected to is the IP that was classified (closing resolve-then-connect / DNS-rebinding TOCTOU). CACHE KEY is (tenant_id, scope, host) - never host alone, because locality depends on the TENANT's declared list and a host-keyed cache would let tenant A's declaration make a host read as local for tenant B. INVALIDATION is explicit and immediate on any mutation of the tenant's declared endpoints, the deployment allowlist, or the tenant/project endpoint settings - a revoked declaration must not keep working for the remainder of the TTL; a revoke-then-call test asserts this. OWNERSHIP AND REFRESH: the cache and its re-resolution are owned by a NAMED SUPERVISED process in the application supervision tree (a periodic task or GenServer with jittered refresh), which re-resolves and re-pins BEFORE expiry and exposes a distinct 'revalidating' state. Without it, TTL expiry is a scheduled fleet-wide self-inflicted outage - every local_only tenant hard-refusing at once - and a privacy control whose steady state is an outage gets disabled in production, which is how the guarantee actually dies. FAIL-CLOSED IS SCOPED, not universal: a stale or missing entry is a fail-closed refusal ONLY for local_only scopes and for tenant-supplied/declared endpoints. Vendor defaults (api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com) are CDN-fronted and rotate, and the default hosted tenant configures nothing and therefore never ran a probe - so for non-local_only scopes on vendor defaults the policy re-resolves normally and pins per request at connect time, preserving AC-41.2.8's and AC-41.6.10's default-off promise. INITIAL POPULATION does not depend on US-41.2 (this story does not depend on it): the policy module populates the cache lazily on first use for today's hardcoded vendor endpoints, and the US-41.2 probe additionally pre-populates it at config time when endpoints become configurable. RECOVERY IS AGENT-REACHABLE: an expired or IP-changed pin returns a DISTINCT :pin_stale error (never conflated with :egress_blocked) whose remediation is a re-pin operation that does NOT require a role :user write - the target deployments (home Ollama box, tailscale funnel, DHCP VPS) change IP routinely, and requiring a human to re-run the role-:user set_llm_config to recover would contradict the epic's agent-native no-UI design principle. A benchmark or timing assertion documents the cached path.

test_cases.name: local_only blocks a vendor endpoint, allows an allowlisted local one
preconditions: scope marked local_only
a loopback endpoint present in the deployment allowlist
steps: attempt an embedding with base_url api.openai.com
attempt one with the allowlisted loopback endpoint
expected_results: first: egress_blocked before any Req.post, nothing sent
second: allowed

test_cases.name: hosted tenant's own public-hostname endpoint is usable via declaration
preconditions: hosted instance
tenant whose endpoint is a public hostname they own
endpoint declared as trusted for purpose 'inference' at role :user
steps: mark the scope local_only
run an embedding
attempt to declare a public hostname whose DNS resolves to 10.0.0.5
attempt a webhook delivery to the inference-only declared host
expected_results: the call is allowed
posture and custody claim label it 'tenant-declared (unverified attestation), not network-local' - never 'network-local'
an UNdeclared public endpoint under the same marking is blocked
EVERY private/loopback/CGNAT/link-local/6PN declaration is REJECTED AT WRITE TIME - a tenant can never carve the operator's network out of the SSRF denylist
the public hostname resolving into a private range is rejected too, at write time and again at pin time
the inference-only host is refused for webhook delivery - declarations are purpose-scoped

test_cases.name: guard survives admission fail-open
preconditions: local_only scope, non-local endpoint
admission backend unavailable so fail_open/2 admits
steps: attempt a provider call
expected_results: still blocked by the egress guard - fail-open must not leak into the privacy decision

test_cases.name: unclassifiable endpoint fails closed
preconditions: local_only scope
classifier forced to raise or return unknown
steps: attempt a provider call
expected_results: refused
reason states the endpoint could not be classified as local

test_cases.name: chokepoint is mandatory, not conventional
preconditions: a fixture module inside the CONFIGURED scanned-path list (AC-41.4.4 ii) containing one raw call per detected entry point: Req.post/request/get/put/patch/delete/new, Req.Request.run, Finch.request, Mint.HTTP, :httpc.request, :gen_tcp.connect, :ssl.connect
steps: run the static/Credo egress check against the fixture path
run it against lib/ as shipped
expected_results: the check FAILS on EVERY entry point in the fixture - a fixture outside the scanned paths would make this control a no-op, so the path list is configurable
it passes on lib/ as shipped - proving both directions
the documented residual gap (HTTP inside a dependency, and the separate mcp-server/ codebase) is stated in the docs, not implied away

test_cases.name: role asymmetry on the local_only flag
preconditions: agent, orchestrator and user keys
a scope currently local_only
a second scope on VENDOR default endpoints, i.e. the state of every existing tenant
steps: attempt to ENABLE at each role
attempt to CLEAR at each role
as orchestrator, ENABLE on the vendor-endpoint scope with no acknowledgement flag
retry with the flag
expected_results: agent cannot enable or clear
orchestrator can enable but NOT clear
user can do both
both transitions appear in the audit log

the pre-flight fires on the vendor-endpoint scope: the un-acknowledged enable is refused (or completes only with the flag) and the response NAMES every endpoint that would become egress_blocked - never a silent tenant-wide outage undoable only by a human
the enable emits the high-priority audit event and the alertable telemetry event

test_cases.name: allowlist is not writable at any role
preconditions: agent, orchestrator and user keys
steps: attempt to modify the deployment allowlist through every exposed tool and endpoint
expected_results: no path mutates it at any role - including :user

test_cases.name: scope precedence is most-restrictive-wins
preconditions: tenant local_only on/off x project local_only on/off
an article with no project
steps: attempt a provider call in each combination
expected_results: blocked whenever EITHER scope is local_only
a project can never relax a tenant marking
the project-less row follows the tenant marking

test_cases.name: posture report is complete and leaks nothing
preconditions: tenant with configured endpoints, declared trusted endpoints and keys
agent, user and orchestrator keys
steps: call egress_posture at role :agent
call it at role :user
expected_results: at :agent: the caller's own endpoints, their locality verdicts, the tenant's declared list with purposes, per-scope local_only/encrypt_body and any named posture defects are present

at :agent the deployment allowlist CONTENTS are ABSENT - only a boolean saying whether a verdict came from the allowlist; operator infrastructure is not disclosed to the lowest-privileged key of every tenant
at :user the allowlist contents are present
no key material anywhere in either payload

test_cases.name: interactive search degrades legibly and does not open the breaker
preconditions: local_only scope with a non-local embedding endpoint
steps: run several semantic searches
inspect telemetry and breaker state
expected_results: keyword fallback with meta naming egress_blocked and the offending endpoint
HTTP 200, never a 500
no [:loopctl, :llm, :provider_error] events
the per-tenant circuit breaker stays closed

test_cases.name: degraded-response meta contract is present and extensible
preconditions: scope with local_only
a non-local embedding endpoint
encrypt_body does NOT exist yet - it ships in US-41.6, which depends on this story
steps: run a semantic search
expected_results: response meta states egress_blocked and names the offending endpoint
the reserved excluded_tiers field is present and empty

test_cases.name: pin cache is tenant-scoped, refreshed and invalidated - and recovery is agent-reachable
preconditions: tenant A with a declared public endpoint
tenant B with no declaration for the same host
a default tenant on vendor endpoints that never ran a probe
steps: classify the host for both tenants
revoke tenant A's declaration and immediately call again
advance time past the TTL for a declared endpoint
change the declared host's DNS to a new public IP
make a provider call as the default tenant
expected_results: tenant A's declaration never makes the host local for tenant B - the cache key is (tenant_id, scope, host)
the revoke invalidates immediately; the declaration does not keep working for the rest of the TTL
the supervised refresher re-pins before expiry - TTL rollover is not a fleet-wide simultaneous refusal
an IP change surfaces a DISTINCT :pin_stale error, never :egress_blocked, with a remediation that re-pins WITHOUT a role :user write
the default tenant is unaffected: no probe, no cache entry, no refusal - AC-41.2.8 / AC-41.6.10 default-off preserved

test_cases.name: egress_blocked is terminal for Oban and bounded in the audit log
preconditions: a permanently local_only-blocked scope
a batch of embedding/extraction jobs for it
steps: enqueue the batch
let it drain
inspect the job table, the audit log and telemetry
expected_results: every job is cancelled ({:cancel, :egress_blocked}) - no retries, no backoff, no queue backlog rebuilt on the next write
the audit log holds a bounded, aggregated set of blocked records per (scope, endpoint, reason, window) with occurrence counts - not one row per call
a [:loopctl, :egress, :blocked] telemetry event and blocked-rate counter reflect the exact per-call rate
no [:loopctl, :llm, :provider_error] events and the breaker stays closed

test_cases.name: capabilities discoverable pre-auth
preconditions: no credentials
steps: GET .well-known/loopctl
expected_results: supported dimensions, tenant-endpoint support and tier list present
no tenant-specific data leaked

test_cases.name: marking state is tenant-isolated
preconditions: two tenants, one with local_only set
steps: read and attempt to mutate tenant A's marking as tenant B
expected_results: not visible, not mutable - RLS policy enforced

technical_notes: The guard lives at ONE wrapper (AC-41.4.4), not replicated at anthropic.ex:118 / embedding_client.ex:91,101 by convention. Those sites call the wrapper; the static check keeps future call sites from bypassing it. Admission stays a separate with-clause so the two failure modes never share a code path.

Classification resolves the endpoint HOST and pins the resulting IPs (AC-41.4.12), so DNS pointing a public name at a private address (or rebinding between resolve and connect) cannot fool it. Reuse UrlGuard.pinned_request_opts/1 rather than inventing a second mechanism. The pin cache is a named, SUPERVISED owner with jittered pre-expiry refresh; a TTL that can only be renewed by a human re-running a role-:user write is an outage schedule, not a control.

This story covers MODEL-PROVIDER egress only. Webhook delivery bypasses Admission entirely (webhooks/req_delivery.ex:43) and is handled in US-41.5 - the docs and the posture report must NOT claim total egress control until 41.5 lands.

egress_posture is a read tool and should be available at agent role: an agent must be able to check locality with the key it already has, or the whole verify-before-harvest workflow fails. WRITING local_only is a different matter - see AC-41.4.1's asymmetric roles.

Record egress_blocked decisions in the audit log - US-41.7 turns these records into the custody claim - but AGGREGATED per (scope, endpoint, reason, window) with an occurrence count, per AC-41.4.6. An unbounded per-call write is a self-inflicted write amplifier: blocking is cheap and happens before any network call, so one misconfigured harvest loop would otherwise flood the audit path. The exact per-call rate lives in the [:loopctl, :egress, :blocked] telemetry counter, not in audit rows.

Dependency note: this story deliberately does NOT depend on US-41.2/US-41.3. Implement the classifier, guard, policy module and posture surface against today's resolved endpoints; extend the resolution inputs when configurable endpoints land.
